title: Mixed-precision accumulation ordering + fallback kernel path causing KV-store desynchronization and decode-time corruption
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Summary: We observed deterministic output divergence and downstream token corruption when a low-latency fallback kernel path is triggered for certain attention configurations. The fault surface appears at the intersection of mixed-precision accumulation ordering differences (fp16->fp32 accumulation) and concurrent prefill/decode scheduling that interleaves writes to the per-request KV index map. The end result is previously-seen tokens reappearing in decode outputs, occasional invalid token IDs, and model perplexity regressions for affected request shapes.

This ticket owns the investigation, repro artifact, short-term mitigation, and a correctness-first rollout for the fix.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start inference server with runtime-1.20 branch and quantization profile qp-3 (int8 emulation + fp16 accumulation).
2) Send mixed-length prefill batch: two requests with prefix length 512 and three short requests (prefix 64) in rapid succession using continuous-batch mode.
3) Ensure kernel selector policy uses cost-based fallback for attention type 'sparse_block' on GPU A100 for seq_len 2048 case (this forces fallback fused attention kernel).
4) Trigger concurrent decode streams that append tokens to the same per-GPU KV slab under high QPS.
5) Observe outputs: duplicated tokens from previous sequences, occasional token ID > vocab_size, and higher perplexity vs baseline.

Repro-rate: ~30% for synthetic workload; 3-5% for production-like traces.
investigation_notes:
- Initial suspicion was a pure memory corruption bug; however ASAN runs on CPU-only reproduced divergence with deterministic pattern pointing at arithmetic ordering differences.
- Bitwise comparison against golden model shows differences in softmax logits at 1e-3 to 1e-2 which amplify during autoregressive decode causing token drift.
- Root cause chain: 1) fallback fused attention kernel uses fp32 accumulation ordering (sum-then-normalize) while optimized path uses pairwise Kahan-style compensation in fp16->fp32 accumulation. 2) Numerical drift changes attention weights marginally. 3) Prefill/decode scheduler interleaves slab pointer updates when a fallback kernel triggers mid-batch; a non-atomic KV index write can race with the decode path's read, producing an out-of-date pointer for a subsequent token. 4) The read of stale pointer combined with small numerical differences causes out-of-bound read from sparse index table under very specific alignment.
- Logs: observed repeated pattern 'kv_idx_update:seq=42->ptr=0x7fa1b8f' immediately followed by 'kv_read:seq=48->ptr=0x7fa1b8f' for distinct requests. This indicates pointer reuse without versioning checks.
- Memory tools (ubsan/asan) did not always flag because pointer remains in range; corruption manifests as semantic mismatch.
- The bug appears mostly when fallback kernels are used for certain attention sparsity masks and when request batching causes prefill and decode phases to overlap on the same worker thread pool.

Hypothesis validated by: 1) forcing identical accumulation ordering in fallback kernel removes numerical divergence; 2) adding a version tag to KV index and checking on read eliminates token corruption (but is a heavier correctness guard).
proposed_fix:
1) Correctness-first change (short-term): make KV index writes atomic and add a 16-bit version tag per entry. On read, validate tag matches expected request epoch; on mismatch, stall decode and fetch canonical pointer. This is higher-cost but prevents corruption.
2) Medium-term: unify accumulation ordering across all kernel variants; port pairwise compensated accumulation from optimized path into fallback fused kernel to eliminate the numeric drift.
3) Long-term: add deterministic unit tests for accumulation kernels (mixed-precision) and a stress test that simulates interleaved prefill/decode schedules.

Implementation notes: patch will modify kernel API to export a small header with 'accumulation_mode' and add atomic store/compare for index writes. Avoid global locks—use per-slab CAS+version.
rollout_plan:
- Cut hotfix branch runtime-1.20-hotfix/ENG-16840 with atomic KV index + version checks.
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic in eu-west1 for 48 hours, monitor token-level diffs and perplexity vs baseline.
- If stable (no token corruption observed, latency impact <5%), expand to 50% and run full regression tests.
- Merge medium-term accumulation unification in runtime-1.21 after performance validation; drop version-tag overhead post-unification.
- Postmortem and knowledge base entry after full rollout.
